history.dynasty: None (modern; maintained by the Iddipilli family)
history.summary: The Sri Subrahmanya Swamy Temple stands at Kothapeta, Islampet, at the foot of the Indrakeeladri hills in central Vijayawada. It is the city's best-documented standalone temple to Lord Subramanya (Murugan/Kartikeya), distinct from the Subramanya sannidhi inside the Kanaka Durga Temple complex. Local temple tradition holds that the devotee lddhipalli Guruvula Das, after a dream in which Lord Subramanya appeared to him as a serpent, pilgrimaged to the Arupadai Veedu (the six holy abodes of Murugan in Tamil Nadu) and modelled this shrine on the Thiruthani Subramanya Swamy temple; idols of Balasubramanya Swamy and of Valli-Devasena Sametha Subramanya were consecrated with Ashtabandana and Kumbhabhishekam in 1954. The 1954 date and founder narrative are temple-tradition accounts (a 2019 temple blog); the Andhra Pradesh Endowments Department listing confirms the temple as Sri Subrahmanyeswara Swamy Temple, Indrakeeladri, but publishes no founding history. The shrine is unusual for worshipping Subramanya in three forms at one site: Dhandayudhapani (boy form), Murugan with his consorts Valli and Devasena, and a serpent-linked form at a revered anthill, drawing devotees seeking remedies for Naga and marriage-related concerns. Kanchi pontiff Sri Jayendra Saraswathi is recorded to have laid the foundation stone for the flight of steps to the hill shrine.

name: Subramanya Swamy Temple
town_description: Vijayawada, on the Krishna river in coastal Andhra Pradesh, is the state's business capital and second city, headquarters of NTR district. It is the main gateway to the new capital Amaravati and the region's pilgrimage circuit, centred on the Kanaka Durga Temple on Indrakeeladri hill and the Prakasam Barrage across the river.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport, Gannavaram (approx. 23-25 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Vijayawada Junction (approx. 3 km), the principal railhead of the region.
travel.road: Pandit Nehru Bus Station (approx. 3 km). In Kothapeta/Islampet behind the Komala Vilas Hotel hill-top area (520001); ask for the Kothapeta Subramanya temple near Indrakeeladri, as several Subramanya shrines exist in the city. The final approach is through a dense old-city neighbourhood and up a flight of steps; vehicles may need to drop passengers short of the shrine.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for bearable weather; early mornings (5:30-9:00 AM) are best for the climb. Tuesdays and Subramanya Sashti draw larger crowds; choose a normal weekday for a quieter visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: About 5:00 AM to 12:30 PM and 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify — older guides list 5:00 AM-12:00 noon, and one travel site lists 6:00 AM-1:30 PM / 3:30 PM-8:00 PM; plan around the midday closure and confirm on festival days).
